findings.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
findings.mechanism: The clause restricts local cooperation with immigration enforcement by forbidding jails from extending detentions solely to fulfill federal immigration detainers.

analysis.answer: Under current law, individual counties have the authority to decide whether their jails will honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure preempts that local authority by prohibiting any county jail from holding a person beyond their normal release time solely because of such a request.

The measure addresses the practice of local jails holding individuals beyond their standard release time for federal immigration enforcement. The mechanism is a direct prohibition on extending custody solely on the basis of a federal detainer.

The state government gains authority over immigration-related detention policies at the local level. County governments, sheriffs, and jail administrators lose the discretion to choose whether to cooperate with federal immigration detainer requests.
